question: Why did Mark Rothko hand back the fee for murals painted for New York's Four Seasons restaurant?
answer: He saw where they would hang. Commissioned in 1958 for the luxury restaurant in the Seagram Building, he dined there and decided it was a place where the rich came to be seen eating. He returned the money and kept the paintings. Nine of them later went to the Tate in London, arriving the day he died.
move: Ask where your work will end up before you take the money.
ask: Is there a job I would do differently if I pictured exactly where my work will end up?
reference: James E. B. Breslin, Mark Rothko: A Biography, University of Chicago Press, 1993
